governing_question: Is our Stage-14 use of the strongly damaged late Job-1_UEL state methodologically consistent with what Pandey & Kumar actually describe for the MISESERI pre-analysis?

published_facts: Pandey & Kumar (2025), CMES 144(3), 3251-3276 describe Job-1_UEL.inp as a 3-layer UEL model on an initial coarse mesh (h_global = 0.02 mm, 2,906 elements, 2,988 nodes).
Job-1 uses a 2-step loading schedule: Delta u1 = 10^-3 for 500 increments, Delta u2 = 5 x 10^-4 for 1000 increments.
Fig. 6(a) displays the authors' MISESERI error indicator distribution used to identify the region requiring mesh refinement.

Abaqus RemeshingRule (sizingMethod=UNIFORM_ERROR, errorTarget=1.0, refinementFactor=10, minElementSize=0.001, maxElementSize=0.02) produced their published mesh of 13,941 linear quadratic and triangular elements.
project_numerical_evidence: In our numerical implementation, pre-peak and early post-peak states (u <= 0.0080 mm, d_max <= 0.3076) carry >49% far-field error at boundaries and yield over-refined global meshes (57k-71k elements) with zero horizontal ligament bandwidth (w(x > 0.5) = 0).

In our model, only after substantial phase-field damage localization and rupture (u >= 0.00940 mm, d_max >= 0.9833) does the crack corridor error share surge to 86.7% - 95.4%, dropping far-field error to <10.5% and forming a narrow horizontal corridor (w = 0.068 - 0.080 mm) across x in [0.5, 1.0].

Applying the published RemeshingRule to our post-localization state produces an adaptive mesh with 14,483 underlying finite elements (43,449 layered elements), labeled PROJECT_TARGET_LIKE_ADAPTIVE_CANDIDATE (+3.89% relative to published 13,941).
unresolved_literature_details: PUBLISHED_FIG6A_PREANALYSIS_STATE = UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE_DETAIL (The exact author displacement, time frame, damage state d_max, and crack-tip position that generated Fig. 6(a) are omitted in the publication).

ABSOLUTE_LOADING_SEMANTICS_UNRESOLVED (The physical displacement amplitude in millimeters for Job-1 is not explicitly defined in the paper text; TWO_STEP_JOB1_STRUCTURE_REPRODUCED__ABSOLUTE_LOADING_SEMANTICS_UNRESOLVED).

fig6a_identification_audit.caption: Figure 6: Error indicator plots for (a) Mode-I and (b) Mode-II loading
fig6a_identification_audit.project_observation: The closest project-observed morphological correspondence occurs after strong damage localization in our model (u >= 0.00940 mm, d_max >= 0.9833), where bulk unloading focuses MISESERI into the horizontal crack corridor.

job1_loading_schedule_audit.published_increment_schedule: Delta u1 = 10^-3 (500 incs), Delta u2 = 5 x 10^-4 (1000 incs)

methodological_circularity_assessment.circularity_finding: The framework functions as an automated 2-pass offline pre-refinement heuristic. It executes a complete coupled phase-field damage solve on an initial coarse mesh to allow crack formation, unloads the bulk material, and uses the resulting localized stress gradient to mark the refinement corridor. While computationally circular if framed as predictive dynamic crack tracking, it is methodologically faithful to the automated 2-pass architecture published by Pandey & Kumar (2025).

formal_classifications.fidelity_justification: The 2-pass UEL pre-analysis workflow, RemeshingRule configuration, and resulting 14,483 element mesh (+3.89% vs 13,941) are structurally and mechanically faithful to the architecture in Pandey & Kumar (2025). The classification is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED because the published text omits explicit documentation of the exact Job-1 frame/displacement endpoint/damage state used to produce Fig. 6(a).
